{{Short description|Symmetric function invariant of graphs}}
The '''chromatic symmetric function''' is a [[Ring of symmetric functions|symmetric function]] [[Invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] of [[Graph theory|graphs]] studied in [[algebraic graph theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]]. It is the weight [[generating function]] for proper [[graph coloring]]s, and was originally introduced by [[Richard P. Stanley|Richard Stanley]] as a generalization of the [[chromatic polynomial]] of a graph.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Stanley |first=R.P. |authorlink=Richard P. Stanley |date=1995 |title=A Symmetric Function Generalization of the Chromatic Polynomial of a Graph |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=111 |issue=1 |pages=166–194 |doi=10.1006/aima.1995.1020 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708}}</ref>

== Definition ==
For a finite graph <math>G=(V,E)</math> with vertex set <math>V=\{v_1,v_2,\ldots, v_n\}</math>, a ''vertex coloring'' is a function <math>\kappa:V\to C</math> where <math>C</math> is a set of colors. A vertex coloring is called ''proper'' if all adjacent vertices are assigned distinct colors (i.e., <math>\{i,j\}\in E \implies \kappa(i)\neq\kappa(j)</math>). The '''chromatic symmetric function''' denoted <math>X_G(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math> is defined to be the weight generating function of proper vertex colorings of <math>G</math>:<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Saliola |first=Franco |date=October 15, 2022 |title=Lectures on Symmetric Functions with a view towards Hessenberg varieties — Draft |url=https://www.birs.ca/workshops/2022/22w5143/files/Franco%20Saliola/Saliola-Lectures-on-Chromatic-Symmetric-Functions.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221018024159/https://www.birs.ca/workshops/2022/22w5143/files/Franco%20Saliola/Saliola-Lectures-on-Chromatic-Symmetric-Functions.pdf |archive-date=October 18, 2022 |access-date=April 27, 2024}}</ref><math display="block">X_G(x_1,x_2,\ldots):=\sum_{\underset{\text{proper}}{\kappa:V\to\N}}x_{\kappa(v_1)}x_{\kappa(v_2)}\cdots x_{\kappa(v_n)}</math>

== Examples ==
For <math>\lambda</math> a [[Integer partition|partition]], let <math>m_\lambda</math> be the [[Symmetric polynomial#Monomial symmetric polynomials|monomial symmetric polynomial]] associated to <math>\lambda</math>.

=== Example 1: complete graphs ===
Consider the [[complete graph]] <math>K_n</math> on <math>n</math> vertices:

* There are <math>n!</math> ways to color <math>K_n</math> with exactly <math>n</math> colors yielding the term <math>n!x_1\cdots x_n</math>
* Since every pair of vertices in <math>K_n</math> is adjacent, it can be properly colored with no fewer than <math>n</math> colors.

Thus, <math>X_{K_n}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=n!x_1\cdots x_n = n!m_{(1,\ldots,1)}</math>

=== Example 2: a path graph ===
Consider the [[path graph]] <math>P_3</math> of length <math>3</math>:

* There are <math>3!</math> ways to color <math>P_3</math> with exactly <math>3</math> colors, yielding the term <math>6x_1x_2x_3</math>
* For each pair of colors, there are <math>2</math> ways to color <math>P_3</math> yielding the terms <math>x_i^2x_j</math> and <math>x_ix_j^2</math> for <math>i\neq j</math>

Altogether, the chromatic symmetric function of <math>P_3</math> is then given by:<ref name=":1" /><math display="block">X_{P_3}(x_1,x_2,x_3) = 6x_1x_2x_3 + x_1^2x_2 + x_1x_2^2 + x_1^2x_3 + x_1x_3^2 + x_2^2x_3 + x_2x_3^2 = 6m_{(1,1,1)} + m_{(1,2)}</math>

== Properties ==

* Let <math>\chi_G</math> be the chromatic polynomial of <math>G</math>, so that <math>\chi_G(k)</math> is equal to the number of proper vertex colorings of <math>G</math> using at most <math>k</math> distinct colors. The values of <math>\chi_G</math> can then be computed by [[Ring of symmetric functions#Specializations|specializing]] the chromatic symmetric function, setting the first <math>k</math> variables <math>x_i</math> equal to <math>1</math> and the remaining variables equal to <math>0</math>:<ref name=":0" /> <math display="block">X_G(1^k)=X_G(1,\ldots,1,0,0,\ldots)=\chi_G(k)</math>
* If <math>G\amalg H</math> is the disjoint union of two graphs, then the chromatic symmetric function for <math>G\amalg H</math> can be written as a product of the corresponding functions for <math>G</math> and <math>H</math>:<ref name=":0" /><math display="block">X_{G\amalg H}=X_G\cdot X_H</math>
* A ''stable partition'' <math>\pi</math> of <math>G</math> is defined to be a [[set partition]] of vertices <math>V</math> such that each block of <math>\pi</math> is an [[Independent set (graph theory)|independent set]] in <math>G</math>. The type of a stable partition <math>\text{type}(\pi)</math> is the partition consisting of parts equal to the sizes of the [[Connected component (graph theory)|connected components]] of the vertex induced subgraphs. For a partition <math>\lambda\vdash n</math>, let <math>z_\lambda</math> be the number of stable partitions of <math>G</math> with <math>\text{type}(\pi)=\lambda=\langle1^{r_1}2^{r2}\ldots\rangle</math>. Then, <math>X_G</math> expands into the augmented monomial symmetric functions, <math>\tilde{m}_\lambda:=r_1!r_2!\cdots m_\lambda</math> with coefficients given by the number of stable partitions of <math>G</math>:<ref name=":0" /><math display="block">X_G=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}z_\lambda \tilde{m}_\lambda</math>
* Let <math>p_\lambda</math> be the [[Symmetric polynomial#Power-sum symmetric polynomials|power-sum symmetric function]] associated to a partition <math>\lambda</math>. For <math>S\subseteq E</math>, let <math>\lambda(S)</math> be the partition whose parts are the vertex sizes of the connected components of the edge-induced subgraph of <math>G</math> specified by <math>S</math>. The chromatic symmetric function can be expanded in the power-sum symmetric functions via the following formula:<ref name=":0" /><math display="block">X_G=\sum_{S\subseteq E}(-1)^{|S|}p_{\lambda(S)}</math>
* Let <math display="inline">X_G=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}c_\lambda e_\lambda</math> be the expansion of <math>X_G</math> in the basis of [[Elementary symmetric polynomial|elementary symmetric functions]] <math>e_\lambda</math>. Let <math>\text{sink}(G,s)</math> be the number of [[acyclic orientation]]s on the graph <math>G</math> which contain exactly <math>s</math> sinks. Then we have the following formula for the number of sinks:<ref name=":0" /><math display="block">\text{sink}(G,s)=\sum_{\underset{l(\lambda)=s}{\lambda\vdash n}}c_\lambda</math>

== Problems regarding the chromatic symmetric functions ==
There are a number of questions regarding the chromatic symmetric function which have received substantial attention in the literature surrounding them.

=== (3+1)-free conjecture ===
For a partition <math>\lambda</math>, let <math>e_\lambda</math> be the elementary symmetric function associated to <math>\lambda</math>.

A [[partially ordered set]] <math>P</math> is called <math>(3+1)</math>''-free'' if it does not contain a subposet isomorphic to the direct sum of the <math>3</math> element [[Chain (poset)|chain]] and the <math>1</math> element chain. The [[Comparability graph|incomparability graph]] <math>\text{inc}(P)</math> of a poset <math>P</math> is the graph with vertices given by the elements of <math>P</math> which includes an edge between two vertices if and only if their corresponding elements in <math>P</math> are [[Comparability|incomparable]]. The following result was conjectured by [[Richard P. Stanley|Stanley]] and [[John Stembridge|Stembridge]] in 1993 and proven by Tatsuyuki Hikita in 2024<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Hikita |first1=Tatsuyuki |title=A proof of the Stanley-Stembridge conjecture |date=2024 |class=math.CO |eprint=2410.12758 }}</ref>.

'''Theorem''' (Hikita) Let <math>G</math> be the incomparability graph of a <math display="inline">(3+1)</math>-free poset, then <math display="inline">X_G</math> is <math>e</math>-positive.

A weaker positivity result is known for the case of expansions into the basis of [[Schur polynomial|Schur functions]].

'''Theorem''' (Gasharov) Let <math>G</math> be the incomparability graph of a <math display="inline">(3+1)</math>-free poset, then <math display="inline">X_G</math> is <math>s</math>-positive.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gasharov |first=Vesselin |date=1996 |title=Incomparability graphs of (3+1)-free posets are s-positive |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82067232.pdf |journal=[[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]] |volume=157 | issue=1–3 |pages=193–197 |doi=10.1016/S0012-365X(96)83014-7 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In the proof of the theorem above, there is a combinatorial formula for the coefficients of the Schur expansion given in terms of ''<math>P</math>-tableaux'' which are a generalization of [[semistandard Young tableaux]] instead labelled with the elements of <math>P</math>.

== Generalizations ==
There are a number of generalizations of the chromatic symmetric function:

* There is a [[categorification]] of the invariant into a [[homology theory]] which is called ''chromatic symmetric homology.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sazdanovic |first1=Radmila |last2=Yip |first2=Martha |date=2018-02-01 |title=A categorification of the chromatic symmetric function |journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] |series=Series A |volume=154 |pages=218–246 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2017.08.014 |doi-access=free |issn=0097-3165|arxiv=1506.03133 }}</ref> This homology theory is known to be a stronger invariant than the chromatic symmetric function alone.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chandler |first1=Alex |last2=Sazdanovic |first2=Radmila |last3=Stella |first3=Salvatore |last4=Yip |first4=Martha |date=2023-09-01 |title=On the strength of chromatic symmetric homology for graphs |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0196885823000775 |journal=Advances in Applied Mathematics |volume=150 |article-number=102559 |doi=10.1016/j.aam.2023.102559 |issn=0196-8858|arxiv=1911.13297 }}</ref>  The chromatic symmetric function can also be defined for vertex-weighted graphs,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Crew |first1=Logan |title=A Deletion-Contraction Relation for the Chromatic Symmetric Function |date=2020 |arxiv=1910.11859 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2020.103143 |last2=Spirkl |first2=Sophie |journal=[[European Journal of Combinatorics]] |volume=89 |article-number=103143}}</ref> where it satisfies a [[Deletion–contraction formula|deletion-contraction]] property analogous to that of the chromatic polynomial. If the theory of chromatic symmetric homology is generalized to vertex-weighted graphs as well, this deletion-contraction property lifts to a long exact sequence of the corresponding homology theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ciliberti |first=Azzurra |date=2024-01-01 |title=A deletion–contraction long exact sequence for chromatic symmetric homology |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0195669823001051 |journal=[[European Journal of Combinatorics]] |volume=115 |article-number=103788 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2023.103788 |issn=0195-6698|arxiv=2211.00699 }}</ref>
* There is also a [[Quasisymmetric function|quasisymmetric]] refinement of the chromatic symmetric function which can be used to refine the formulae expressing <math>X_G</math> in terms of Gessel's basis of fundamental quasisymmetric functions and the expansion in the basis of Schur functions.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Shareshian |first1=John |last2=Wachs |first2=Michelle L. |authorlink2=Michelle L. Wachs |date=June 4, 2016 |title=Chromatic quasisymmetric functions |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=295 |pages=497–551 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2015.12.018 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708|arxiv=1405.4629 }}</ref>  Fixing an order for the set of vertices, the ascent set of a proper coloring <math>\kappa</math> is defined to be <math>\text{asc}(\kappa)=\{\{i,j\}\in E:i<j \text{ and } \kappa(i)<\kappa(j)\}</math>. The ''chromatic quasisymmetric function'' of a graph <math>G</math> is then defined to be:<ref name=":2" /><math display="block">X_G(x_1,x_2,\ldots;t):=\sum_{\underset{\text{proper}}{\kappa:V\to \N}}t^{|asc(\kappa)|}x_{\kappa(v_1)}\cdots x_{\kappa(v_n)}</math>
